Every piece of electric music gear starts at the wall socket. Most problems (hum, crackles, gear that won't turn
on, blown speakers) and the only really dangerous ones come from how it's powered.

## The order: on last, off first

Speakers and amplifiers make a loud **thump** when anything before them is switched on or off, and big thumps
damage speakers and ears.

- **Switching on**: sources first (keyboards, pedals, mixer, computer, interface), **amplifiers and powered
  speakers last**, volume down.
- **Switching off**: the reverse. **Amps and speakers off first**, then everything else.
- Turn the **volume down** before plugging or unplugging any cable into a live amp.

Easy way to remember: *amps are last on, first off.*

## Sockets, power strips and extension leads

- One wall socket can supply a limited current. In **India** mains is **230 V, 50 Hz**: the small 3-pin socket is
  **6 A** (~1400 W) and the big one **16 A** (in the US 15 A at 120 V; UK/EU 13–16 A at 230 V). Add up the watts printed on each piece of gear; a band's backline plus a PA can get close.
- **Daisy-chaining** power strips into power strips overloads the first one and its cable. One strip per socket.
- **Unroll extension reels fully**: a coiled reel under load heats up and can melt.
- Use strips with a **surge protector** for computers and digital gear; a cheap strip with no breaker is a fire risk.
- **Voltage swings, power cuts and the inverter/generator switching over** send spikes. Where the supply is unsteady,
  run keyboards, mixers and computers through a **stabiliser or UPS**, and switch amps off (or down) before power
  returns after a cut. Many sockets in India have their own switch: turn it off before plugging in.
- Plug adaptors (a 2-pin or UK plug in an Indian socket) often fit loosely and lose the earth: use a proper
  Indian-plug cable or a strip with an earth.
- Keep drinks off amps and mixers, cables out of puddles, and water bottles on the floor, not on the keyboard.

## Earth (ground) and hum

The third pin is the **earth** (ground). It's there so that if something fails inside, the metal case can't become live.

- **Never** break, tape over or remove the earth pin, or use a "ground lift" plug on the power cable, to stop hum.
  That's how musicians have been electrocuted.
- **Hum** (a steady 50 or 60 Hz buzz and its harmonics) usually comes from a **ground loop**: two pieces of gear
  earthed at different sockets and also joined by an audio cable. Fixes, safest first:
  - Power everything that's connected together from the **same** socket or strip.
  - Use **balanced** cables and **DI boxes**; press the DI's **ground lift** switch (that lifts the *audio* shield,
    which is safe; the power earth stays connected).
  - Keep audio cables away from power cables, or cross them at right angles.
  - Laptops on chargers hum through their audio out: try running on battery.
- **Buzz that changes when you touch the strings** on a guitar is shielding or grounding in the guitar or its
  cable, not the wall.

## Power supplies

- **Wall warts** (adaptors) must match the gear: **voltage**, **polarity** (centre positive or negative, shown by a
  little diagram), and at least the **current** (mA) it needs. Wrong voltage or polarity can kill a pedal or keyboard
  instantly. Label every adaptor with what it belongs to.
- **Pedalboards**: an isolated-output power supply is quieter than a daisy-chain cable.
- **Travelling**: 120 V gear (bought in the US) on India's 230 V burns out unless it says "100–240 V". Check the label before using a
  plug adaptor.
- **Batteries**: take them out of pedals and wireless packs when stored; leaking batteries ruin the contacts.
  Unplug the input jack of a battery pedal to switch it off.

## Phantom power and wireless

- **+48 V phantom power** for condenser mics: switch it on with the channel muted and turn it off before unplugging
  ([Recording 2](rec-mics.qmd)).
- **Wireless mics and in-ears**: fresh or fully charged batteries before every show, not "it still had a bar".

## Stay safe

- A tingle from a microphone or guitar strings is a fault: **stop**, unplug, and tell someone in charge.
- Outdoors, and in the monsoon, power must go through an **RCD / RCCB / GFCI** (a breaker that trips on a leak to earth).
- Don't open amps, especially **valve (tube) amps**: they hold lethal voltages after being unplugged.
- Tape cables down or use cable ramps across walkways; trips are the most common injury at gigs.
